newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: U.S. to defend Strait of Hormuz - U.S. commander.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to defend Strait of Hormuz - U.S. commander.

text.p: The United States would take immediate action to defend the Strait of Hormuz against any Iranian threat to close the strategic waterway, a U.S. military commander said.
"We will take immediate action in terms of the defence of the strait," Commander-in-Chief of the U.S. Central Command, General Binford Peay, said in Bahrain, headquarters of the U.S. Fifth Fleet.
His remarks, on Saturday, were released by the U.S. embassy on Sunday, as Iranian air and naval forces launched a new six-day round of wargames in the Gulf.

"Access to the strait is very important, not just to the United States of America, but it is vitally important for the entire world," Peay said when asked about an Iranian threat to close the strait if attacked by Washington.

The commander of Iran's Revolutionary Guards, Major-General Mohsen Rezaei, said after Iranian wargames in April: "We can keep the Strait of Hormuz open...but if we want to, we shall close this strait to anyone who is an obstacle to security in the region and keep it open for our friends and the Moslems."
About 15 million barrels of oil -- half the world's exports -- pass through the 55 km (35 mile) wide strait each day on the way to markets in Asia, Europe and the United States.

Iranian officials have repeatedly said they had no intention of threatening the world's supply of oil and a closure of the the strategic channel between Iran's southern coast and the tip of the Arabian peninsula would shut off Iran's own oil exports, which account for 90 percent of its foreign currency earnings.
The United States has about 20 warships and auxiliary support vessels in the Gulf to protect oil supplies to the West.
"I think you know that enormous amounts of oil transitions pass through...the waters of this region daily, and that these are of vital interest to all of us in the world community," Peay said.
"The United States of America will be a major player in ensuring these straits remain open," he added.
He said the United States had a sizeable naval capacity and "they are very, very highly trained".
"Our navy is the very best in the world...I can assure you that we are going to keep the straits open and no country should pose that kind of aggression in this very important region," he added.
Peay reiterated U.S. accusations that Iran supported terrorism and posed a threat to security in the Gulf. Iran denies both charges.
